_note: Search-only descriptors: appended to each person's embedding text so relational/identity queries work (e.g. 'brother of Musa' -> Harun). Not displayed anywhere; used only to build the semantic search index.
adam: Adam, the first man and the first prophet, the father of all humankind, created by Allah from clay
hawwa: Hawwa (Eve), the wife of Adam and the mother of all humankind
habil: Habil (Abel), the righteous son of Adam who was killed by his own brother Qabil
qabil: Qabil (Cain), the son of Adam who murdered his brother Habil out of envy
iblis: Iblis (Satan, the Devil), who refused to prostrate to Adam and was cast out
idris: Idris (Enoch), an early prophet, a man of truth whom Allah raised to a high station
nuh: Nuh (Noah), the prophet and first great messenger to the people of the earth, who built the ark and survived the flood
son-of-nuh: the son of the prophet Nuh (Noah) who refused to believe and drowned in the flood
wife-of-nuh: the disbelieving wife of the prophet Nuh (Noah)
hud: Hud, the prophet sent to the arrogant people of Ad
the-people-of-ad: the people of Ad, the mighty tribe to whom the prophet Hud was sent
salih: Salih, the prophet sent to the people of Thamud, given the miraculous she-camel as a sign
the-people-of-thamud: Thamud, the people who carved homes in the mountains and hamstrung the she-camel of Salih
ibrahim: Ibrahim (Abraham), the friend of Allah (Khalil-ullah), who broke the idols and was cast into the fire; the father of the prophets Ismail and Ishaq and forefather of Muhammad
azar: Azar, the idol-carving father of the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham)
the-king-nimrud: Nimrud (Nimrod), the tyrant king who argued with Ibrahim and cast him into the fire
sarah: Sarah, the wife of the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and the mother of Ishaq (Isaac)
hajar: Hajar (Hagar), the wife of Ibrahim and mother of Ismail, who ran between Safa and Marwah seeking water at Makkah
the-tyrant-of-egypt: the tyrant king of Egypt who coveted Sarah, the wife of Ibrahim
ismail: Ismail (Ishmael), the prophet, the elder son of Ibrahim and Hajar, offered in sacrifice; the forefather of the Prophet Muhammad
ishaq: Ishaq (Isaac), the prophet, the son of Ibrahim and Sarah, and the father of Yaqub
lut: Lut (Lot), the prophet and nephew of Ibrahim, sent to the people who committed abominations
wife-of-lut: the disbelieving wife of the prophet Lut (Lot), who perished with the wrongdoers
the-people-of-lut: the people of Lut (Lot), the town destroyed for its abominations
the-angel-guests: the angels who came to Lut and Ibrahim disguised as guests
shuayb: Shuayb (Jethro), the prophet sent to the people of Madyan who cheated in weights and measures
the-people-of-madyan: the people of Madyan, sent the prophet Shuayb, who cheated in trade
elder-of-midian: the elder of Madyan whose daughter the prophet Musa married
ayyub: Ayyub (Job), the prophet renowned for his patience through severe affliction and loss
wife-of-ayyub: the loyal wife of the prophet Ayyub (Job) who cared for him through his affliction
yusuf: Yusuf (Joseph), the prophet, the beloved son of Yaqub, cast into a well by his brothers, sold into Egypt, and raised to power
yaqub: Yaqub (Jacob, Israel), the prophet, the son of Ishaq and the father of Yusuf and his eleven brothers
binyamin: Binyamin (Benjamin), the youngest full brother of the prophet Yusuf (Joseph)
brothers-of-yusuf: the ten half-brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) who cast him into the well out of envy
al-aziz: al-Aziz, the Egyptian minister who bought Yusuf and raised him in his house
wife-of-al-aziz: the wife of al-Aziz (Zulaykha), who tried to seduce Yusuf in Egypt
king-of-egypt: the King of Egypt whose dream Yusuf interpreted, raising him to power
musa: Musa (Moses), the prophet to whom Allah spoke directly (Kalim-ullah); he confronted Pharaoh, led the Children of Israel out of Egypt, parted the sea, and received the Torah; the brother of Harun
harun: Harun (Aaron), the elder brother of the prophet Musa (Moses); a prophet himself, appointed as Musa's helper and spokesman
mother-of-musa: the mother of the prophet Musa (Moses), who cast her infant into the river to save him from Pharaoh
sister-of-musa: the sister of the prophet Musa (Moses), who followed his basket along the river
firawn: Firawn (Pharaoh), the tyrant king of Egypt who claimed to be a god and oppressed the Children of Israel, drowned in the sea
wife-of-firawn: Asiya, the believing wife of Pharaoh who rejected his tyranny and is among the greatest women
as-samiri: as-Samiri, the man who led the Children of Israel astray by fashioning the golden calf
magicians-of-firawn: the magicians of Pharaoh who believed in Musa after their staffs were overcome
al-khidr: al-Khidr, the servant of Allah given hidden knowledge, whom Musa journeyed to learn from
dawud: Dawud (David), the prophet-king who slew the giant Jalut (Goliath), was given the Zabur (Psalms) and a beautiful voice, and was the father of Sulayman
jalut: Jalut (Goliath), the giant tyrant-warrior slain by the young Dawud with a sling
talut: Talut (Saul), the king appointed over the Children of Israel to fight Jalut
sulayman: Sulayman (Solomon), the prophet-king, the son of Dawud, given power over the wind, the jinn, and the speech of birds and ants; judged between the two women
bilqis: Bilqis, the Queen of Sheba (Saba), who ruled Yemen and submitted to Allah with Sulayman
the-jinn-of-sulayman: the jinn made subject to the prophet-king Sulayman, who built and dived for him
ilyas: Ilyas (Elijah), the prophet who called his people away from the idol Baal to worship Allah alone
people-of-ilyas: the people to whom Ilyas was sent, who worshipped the idol Baal
alyasa: al-Yasa (Elisha), the prophet, the companion and successor of Ilyas among the Children of Israel
dhulkifl: Dhul-Kifl, a patient and righteous prophet named among the best in the Qur'an
yunus: Yunus (Jonah), the prophet who was swallowed by the great fish and cried out in the darkness; his people believed and were spared
the-people-of-nineveh: the people of Nineveh, the town of the prophet Yunus that believed and was spared
zakariyya: Zakariyya (Zechariah), the aged prophet and guardian of Maryam, whose prayer for a son was answered with Yahya
yahya: Yahya (John the Baptist), the prophet, the son of Zakariyya, given wisdom as a child; the cousin who confirmed Isa
maryam: Maryam (Mary), the chaste and chosen virgin, the mother of the prophet Isa (Jesus), the greatest of women
isa: Isa (Jesus), the prophet and Messiah, the son of Maryam (Mary), a word from Allah and a spirit from Him; not crucified but raised to Allah, and to return
the-disciples: the disciples (al-Hawariyyun), the loyal followers and supporters of the prophet Isa (Jesus)
abd-al-muttalib: Abd al-Muttalib, the grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad who raised him as an orphan
abu-talib: Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet Muhammad who protected and defended him though he did not accept Islam
abu-bakr: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, the closest companion and dearest friend of the Prophet Muhammad, his companion in the cave during the Hijrah, and the first caliph after him
umar: Umar ibn al-Khattab, the mighty companion of the Prophet Muhammad and the second caliph
uthman: Uthman ibn Affan, the modest and generous companion of the Prophet and the third caliph
ali-ibn-abi-talib: Ali ibn Abi Talib, the young cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad, who slept in his bed during the Hijrah; the fourth caliph
hamza: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the uncle of the Prophet Muhammad, the Lion of Allah, martyred at the Battle of Uhud
al-abbas: al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, an uncle of the Prophet Muhammad
khadijah: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, the first wife of the Prophet Muhammad and the very first person to believe in him
aisha: Aisha, the wife of the Prophet Muhammad and the daughter of Abu Bakr, a great scholar among the companions
waraqah: Waraqah ibn Nawfal, the learned cousin of Khadijah who recognized the first revelation to the Prophet
bilal: Bilal ibn Rabah, the formerly enslaved Abyssinian companion, tortured for his faith, who became the first muezzin
abu-jahl: Abu Jahl, one of the fiercest enemies of the Prophet Muhammad among Quraysh, killed at the Battle of Badr
abu-sufyan: Abu Sufyan, a leader of Quraysh who long opposed the Prophet and later accepted Islam at the Conquest of Makkah
an-najashi: the Negus (an-Najashi), the just Christian king of Abyssinia who gave refuge to the persecuted Muslims
ja-far: Jafar ibn Abi Talib, the cousin of the Prophet who spoke for the Muslims before the Negus in Abyssinia and was martyred at Mutah
zayd-ibn-harithah: Zayd ibn Harithah, the freed slave beloved of the Prophet, and a commander martyred at Mutah
khalid-ibn-al-walid: Khalid ibn al-Walid, the brilliant military commander called 'the Sword of Allah'
abdullah-ibn-rawahah: Abdullah ibn Rawahah, the poet-companion and commander martyred at the Battle of Mutah
musab-ibn-umayr: Musab ibn Umayr, the young companion sent ahead to teach Islam in Madinah, martyred at Uhud
salman-al-farisi: Salman al-Farisi, the Persian companion who advised digging the trench at the Battle of the Confederates
sad-ibn-muadh: Sad ibn Muadh, the leader of the Aws in Madinah, whose judgement was passed on Banu Qurayza
kab-ibn-malik: Kab ibn Malik, the companion and poet who stayed behind from Tabuk and whose repentance was accepted
nusaybah: Nusaybah bint Kab (Umm Umarah), the woman who defended the Prophet with her body at Uhud
safiyyah: Safiyyah, an aunt of the Prophet Muhammad
asma-bint-abi-bakr: Asma bint Abi Bakr, the daughter of Abu Bakr who carried provisions to the cave during the Hijrah
suraqah: Suraqah ibn Malik, who chased the Prophet and Abu Bakr during the Hijrah until his horse sank in the sand
suhayl-ibn-amr: Suhayl ibn Amr, the Quraysh envoy who negotiated the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
mutim-ibn-adi: Mutim ibn Adi, the Makkan who granted the Prophet protection on his return from Taif
